text:
omar: Heads up — PR #8129 landed to canary and we're seeing ~12% p95 regression on 8k longseq. Can someone take quick eyes? https://git/repo/pull/8129 :eyes:
perf-bot: Canary run 2690012000 results: p95=202ms (+12% vs baseline 180ms), p50=32ms, peak_rss +60MB. Details: https://bench/2690012
lia: On it. Which canary config was used? microbatching toggled?
ben: PR touches kv-eviction + batch scheduler. Suspect kv-shard merge. Repro command I used locally:
```
run_bench --model longseq --seq 8192 --concurrency 16 --microbatch false
```
tejas: I can run a local microbench in ~20m. If it's kv-shard, we can try reverting shard_count to 8 as a quick experiment.
marie: If we plan to rollback, what's the blast radius? Any errors in canary?
omar: No auth or 5xx spikes, just tail latency. Canary logs show elevated GC around token ~2048. Snippet:
```
2026-05-08T14:02:12Z INFO kv_merge: allocated temp_buf 12MB
2026-05-08T14:02:12Z WARN gc: consider-sweep triggered, paused 18ms
2026-05-08T14:02:13Z INFO request: latency 212ms p95
```
ben: Pushed a flamegraph from the canary run: https://perf/graphs/8129 — kv_merge and buffer_alloc dominate tail.
lia: If GC/alloc is the culprit, the new allocator path might be introducing extra mem pressure for long sequences. Can we toggle quantized kernel fallback for the canary patch to test?
tejas: Ran the repro: baseline p95 178ms -> patch p95 201ms, peak RSS +58MB. Repro steps match ben's command. Looks like extra buffer in kv-merge. PR #8129 is the likely cause.
omar: Ok. Need quick approvals to either rollback or merge a mitigation. Ben — can you approve a rollback? Lia — can you +1 if you agree to revert while we follow up? @ben @lia
ben: Approving rollback now. :thumbsup:
lia: +1. Also request a follow-up: add a microbenchmark for longseq in CI and a guard that fails on >5% p95 regression.
deploy-bot: Scheduled rollback to canary at 2690013000 (in ~8m). Rolling back PR #8129 -> target canary.
marie: Thanks. SRE: please monitor p95 and error rates during rollback window and ping this thread if anything abnormal. I'll create a short dashboard watch and notify paging if needed.
